definition: To accompany someone somewhere for protection, guidance, or as part of a formal arrangement.
etymology: From French escorte, from Italian scorta, meaning a guard or protection.

definition: To go somewhere with someone or to exist or occur together with something else.
etymology: From Old French acompaignier, meaning to associate with or join.

definition: Suggesting that someone or something may cause harm or danger.
etymology: From menace + -ing, from Latin minaciae, meaning threats.

definition: To move downward, especially from a higher position to a lower one.
etymology: From Latin descendere, meaning to climb down or go down.

definition: A person training for a military or other uniformed service.
etymology: From French cadet, meaning younger son or junior member.

translations.uz: yangi askar; ishga olmoq; jalb qilmoq

definition: A new member of an organization or group; to persuade or employ someone to join.
etymology: From French recrute, from recroître, meaning to grow again or replenish.

definition: To defeat someone by using greater intelligence or cleverness.
etymology: From out- (to surpass) + wit (mental ability or intelligence).

definition: A position of high importance, rank, or reputation.
etymology: From Latin eminentia, meaning prominence or high position.

definition: The state of being important, famous, or easily noticed.
etymology: From Latin prominentia, meaning projecting or standing out.

definition: To put someone in prison or keep them confined.
etymology: From Old French emprisonner, from prison.

definition: To cause someone to experience something unpleasant, harmful, or painful.
etymology: From Latin infligere, meaning to strike against or impose.

definition: To a large degree or extent.
etymology: From great + -ly.

translations.uz: qadam; sur'at; u yoqdan bu yoqqa yurmoq

definition: The speed at which something happens or someone moves; to walk back and forth, especially while thinking or waiting.
etymology: From Latin passus, meaning step or pace, through Old French.

definition: In a way that shows a lack of breath, usually because of excitement, fear, or physical effort.
etymology: From breathless + -ly, from breath + -less.

definition: A picture made with paint; the activity of applying paint to a surface.
etymology: From paint + -ing, from Old French peint, meaning painted.

definition: Extremely beautiful, delicate, or carefully made.
etymology: From Latin exquisitus, meaning carefully sought out or select.

definition: Easily damaged, or having a fine, subtle, or gentle quality.
etymology: From Latin delicatus, meaning delightful, refined, or luxurious.

definition: To prevent someone or something from being harmed or lost; to keep something for future use.
etymology: From Old French sauver, from Latin salvare, meaning to make safe.
